description:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

💜 The role

Women's bodies are different, yet medicine still treats them the same. Women get diagnosed about 4 years later than men on average across 700+ types of disease. In France, 51% of women say a health professional has played down their symptoms at least once.

We want to change that. We are building the health system women never had: one that listens to women, anticipates their needs at every stage of life instead of waiting for problems to appear, and gives them care they can trust. To do this, we combine the latest evidence, digital tools, AI and carefully selected health professionals with our strength as an insurer.

We are looking for a doctor who wants to do medicine differently: to build products that thousands of women use and that address their needs; to move care towards prevention; and to work every day with people who think differently, such as product managers, designers, engineers and marketers.

As our Clinical Lead for Women's Health, you make this clinically credible and effective. You own the clinical choices, and you are an essential and active contributor in the product team.

A few things to know before you apply

  • This is a clinical role inside a product team, at an early stage. You own the clinical choices and you build the product with project builder, engineers, designers, ... A good product combines many factors, and the clinical side is one of them. There is a lot to build, to test and to change, and not everything is proven yet. For example, we measure how much our services are used much better than the health outcomes they achieve: building that measurement, honestly, is part of the job.

  • You work outside the usual medical world. Most of your colleagues are not health professionals. You will confront perspectives, explain clinical constraints in simple words, listen to product and business constraints, and find solutions together. Decisions are discussed and made as a team.

  • It takes real time. We prefer 80% or more; at least 60% is possible.

What you will do

You will be the clinical lead of our Women's Health offer, and you will help turn it into a product that women use and trust.

  • Build the product with the team. Work closely with product managers, designers and engineers, and bring the clinical view early, when it shapes decisions, not at the end. With AI tools, you can also build simple things yourself, without knowing how to code.

  • Own the clinical choices. Define our clinical positions based on evidence, design protocols and care pathways, and hold a few clear, explained red lines. When something doesn't work, you help find a safe and relevant alternative.

  • Make our AI safe and accurate on women's health. Work with the product team on how Mo, our AI-powered health companion, handles women's health topics, and help evaluate and improve it.

  • Show the value for women. Help define how we measure the impact on women's health, using evidence-based tools and value-based healthcare principles.

  • Work with our Clinic team. Work hand in hand with Alan's doctors, midwives and other health professionals: help train and support them, and be the person they turn to for difficult cases.

  • Feed and endorse our medical communication. Make sure what we say about women's health is accurate and evidence-based, and help explain it in simple words. Over time, you may represent Alan on these topics.

What success looks like in 6 months

  • Product: you are a core member of the product team, and the first member journeys reflect your clinical input from the start.

  • Protocols in use: the clinical protocols and care pathways of our first women's health program are validated and applied by the Clinic team.

  • Clinic team: midwives and doctors on the program are trained on the protocols, clinical staffing is under way, and you supervise complex cases.

  • Health outcomes: the program's health outcomes are defined and tracked.

  • AI quality: you have helped us make sure our AI handles women's health safely and accurately.

What this role is not

  • Not a medical advisor or reviewer who comes in at the end, nor the person who decides alone.

  • Not the person who runs all the consultations: our midwives and doctors do that, and you design, pilot and supervise.

  • Not an expert on every topic: you bring in other health professionals when needed.

A dynamic, international community of health professionals

You don't work alone. You join Alan's health professionals community: a large network of doctors, midwives, psychologists and other clinicians in France, Spain, Belgium and Canada, and a small core team of Alaners, other clinical leads working on different health programs or services. It is a community with high standards, direct and caring feedback, and a lot of room to shape things.

Beyond Women's Health, you will:

  • Share your practice and learn from others through case reviews and community sessions;

  • Help set common standards across programs;

  • Help welcome, train and mentor new health professionals joining Alan;

  • Help other teams at Alan understand key health concepts, such as evidence-based care;

  • Over time, contribute to other health topics beyond Women's Health.

👀 Is it you we're looking for?

Must-haves

  • You are a gynecologist (OB-GYN) or a GP with solid training in women's health, for example a university diploma (DU or DIU) in gynecology, or several years of regular gynecological follow-up in your practice. You can come from private practice, a hospital, a clinic or a health tech company.

  • At least 5 years of post-residency experience, with solid clinical judgment and evidence-based prescribing.

  • Clinical experience across several areas of women's health, for example contraception, fertility, endometriosis, menopause or hormone treatments.

  • An open, pragmatic mindset: you enjoy working with non-medical teams, you make trade-offs when they are legitimate while defending evidence-based rigor, and you are curious about what AI and digital tools change in medicine.

  • Outcomes thinking: you care about the results that matter to patients compared with what care costs (value-based healthcare), and about prevention, not only treatment.

  • A great understanding of the French healthcare system.

  • Fluency in both French and English.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience training or supervising other health professionals is a plus, and a collaborative approach with midwives, dietitians, therapists, …

  • Experience in digital health, a start-up, a healthcare project or teleconsultation.

  • Experience writing or contributing to a clinical protocol or guideline.

🤝 How we work

  • Contract: you join Alan as an employee, ideally at 80% or more, and at least 60%. You can keep some clinical practice outside Alan.

  • Team: you are part of the Women's Health product team and of Alan's health professionals community.

  • Location: our headquarters are in Paris. You can be based abroad, as long as you speak French fluently and know the French healthcare system well.

  • Remote work: we offer remote work flexibility, but we value in-person collaboration.

🔄 What to expect from our recruitment process

  1. Application Review: we read your CV and application.

  2. Screening interview (45 to 60 minutes): your path, your motivation for this role, and practical points such as your availability.

  3. Technical interview: a short written case at home (60 to 90 minutes), including a situation where clinical and product needs conflict, then a live discussion of your answers.

  4. Alaner Fit interview: a conversation about how we work at Alan and whether it suits you.

  5. Alan Day: an on-site day where you prepare concrete use cases, present them to a panel and meet the people you would work with.

  6. Reference calls, including at least one with a non-medical colleague you have worked with.

Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman: did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

💡 You want to know more about Alan?

  • Perks & Benefits: Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

  • A strong culture: People joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. We have a set of cultural values that guide our approach to work.

  • Check out our About Alan and Career pages for more info.
